assessment: Four technically feasible intervention families. No defensible company-wide 2031 adoption or investable reduction total from public inputs collected. Unit-process and historical normalized scenarios are computable, explicitly conditional.
baseline_policy: Use FY2026 fixed operational service volumes, preserving separate CY2025 waste period. Do not infer activity from revenue intensity. All adoption quantities are null pending asset data.

interventions.name: Leak prevention and lower-GWP equipment replacement
interventions.technology_available: Leak detection, preventive maintenance, trained technicians and commercial CO2 systems; choose leak repair or equipment replacement for each system, not additive independent full reductions.

activity_baseline.lifecycle_boundary: onsite refrigerants Scope 1; excludes electricity and equipment manufacture

evidence.unit: US facilities partially or fully using ultra-low-GWP refrigerants
evidence.lifecycle_boundary: deployment count, not refrigerant-charge or cooling-capacity share

evidence.unit: annual leak fraction (individual stores below this demonstrated)
evidence.lifecycle_boundary: operational refrigerant loss; advanced technology plus practices, not leakage-only causal estimate

evidence.geography: global physical factor; US regulatory table
global physical factor; US regulatory table

interventions.fixed_activity_formula: For each system at fixed baseline cooling service: direct avoided kgCO2e = charge0_kg*leak0*GWP0 - charge1_kg*leak1*GWP1. Add metered electricity delta times a consistent grid factor; separately count installation/end-of-life recovery losses. Aggregate only verified adopted systems.

bounded_scenario.kind: unit-process arithmetic, not company reduction or adoption forecast
bounded_scenario.functional_unit: 1 kg/year of verified avoided R-404A leakage
bounded_scenario.counterfactual: Same cooling service and equipment; leakage would otherwise continue. No electricity credit.
bounded_scenario.replacement_sensitivity: At equal emitted mass, substitution of 1 kg R-404A by 1 kg CO2 reduces direct emissions by 3.921 tCO2e. Equal leakage mass is only a sensitivity, not an engineering forecast.

interventions.repayable_mechanism: Shared-savings maintenance contract from documented avoided refrigerant purchases/repair costs; equipment lease only when net utility and maintenance savings or contracted service payments cover debt.
interventions.additionality: Existing corporate replacement schedule and required compliance are baseline. Finance must demonstrably accelerate specific assets or address a documented procurement/skills bottleneck.
dependencies: system charge/gas composition and actual leak logs
capex, remaining asset life and incremental opex
overlaps: Do not add full leak-repair savings to full gas-replacement savings for the same charge.
Electricity changes belong once in energy ledger.

interventions.name: Residual legacy lighting replacement and controls
interventions.technology_available: Commercial LEDs and controls; only applicable where a current audit finds eligible legacy fixtures.

evidence.baseline: 2012 new-site LED design versus respectively 400 W and 1000 W pulse-start metal-halide alternatives
evidence.lifecycle_boundary: use-phase parking-lot electricity; not whole building or embodied energy
historical project cost/energy/maintenance comparison; not financing IRR

interventions.fixed_activity_formula: Eligible baseline lighting kWh * verified savings fraction; constant lit service and operating hours. Scope2 benefit = saved kWh * consistent site grid/contract emission factor.

bounded_scenario.kind: normalized historical engineering scenario, not Walmart remaining stock
bounded_scenario.functional_unit: 100 MWh/year of eligible legacy parking-lot lighting under the source comparator conditions
bounded_scenario.basis: 100 MWh * 44% or 63%; savings kWh * historical USD0.056/kWh. Endpoints are different comparator designs, not statistical confidence limits.
bounded_scenario.excluded: Current tariffs, emissions factors, current installed stock, capex, financing costs and current realized payback unknown.

interventions.repayable_mechanism: Equipment lease or energy-performance contract repaid from metered net utility and maintenance savings; audit first.
interventions.additionality: This may already be largely exhausted at Walmart. No investable volume assumed from an old successful demonstration.
overlaps: Renewable electricity procurement and efficiency cannot each claim the original same kWh emissions.
Refrigeration/HVAC energy effects require separate measurement.

interventions.name: Electric yard tractors for verified compatible duty cycles
interventions.technology_available: Battery-electric yard trucks already deployed; site operations are more bounded than long-haul trucking.

evidence.unit: fraction reduction exceeded per operating hour
evidence.geography: Walmart distribution/fulfillment operations; exact trial sites undisclosed
evidence.baseline: electric yard trucks versus diesel yard equipment, FY2026 disclosure
evidence.lifecycle_boundary: corporate claimed emissions per hour; electricity methodology and vehicle lifecycle boundary not disclosed

interventions.fixed_activity_formula: Verified baseline yard-hours * (diesel emissions per hour minus electric electricity per hour * consistent grid factor), with equal task output and uptime; report vehicle/battery manufacturing separately.
interventions.repayable_mechanism: Truck/charger lease funded by net avoided fuel and maintenance expenditure, subject to tariff, utilization and replacement-cost diligence.
interventions.additionality: Subtract already ordered electrification and corporate investment. No blanket application of the reported percentage to total fleet emissions.
dependencies: remaining diesel yard count and hours
charging interconnection capacity and demand charges
overlaps: Do not apply yard factor to long-haul tractors or mobile refrigerants.
Electricity enters Scope2; renewable claim must use same ledger.

interventions.name: Prevent spoilage and use higher-value recovery pathways
interventions.technology_available: Forecasting, inventory visibility, markdowns, cold-chain monitoring, and de-packaging/recovery are deployed technologies. Prevention and disposal diversion need separate outcomes.

evidence.unit: million lb food/year sent to landfill or incineration
evidence.geography: global operational Walmart food reporting, excluding India
evidence.lifecycle_boundary: operational food destination mass; not edible share, upstream lifecycle emissions or US-only volume

evidence.unit: US locations exceeded by de-packaging deployment

evidence.baseline: versus prior recovery at participating sites; raw protocol undisclosed
evidence.lifecycle_boundary: recovered mass, not food prevented or GHG reduction

evidence.baseline: versus prior trash at participating sites; raw protocol undisclosed
evidence.lifecycle_boundary: trash mass, not total food waste

evidence.geography: grocery subset geography not separately disclosed; study spans 17 countries
evidence.baseline: historical grocery waste projects reported by 2017; 10 sites
evidence.lifecycle_boundary: project-period tangible financial flows; not annual ROI or lifecycle GHG factor

interventions.fixed_activity_formula: Hold food-service output/product mix constant. Prevented kg * commodity-specific upstream marginal factor only if procurement/production actually falls; rerouted kg * difference between geographically appropriate waste-treatment factors, including energy, methane capture and transport.
interventions.repayable_mechanism: Working-capital/process-improvement loan or shared-savings contract funded by verified lower write-offs, net markdown margin, avoided purchasing and disposal bills. Do not assume food donation creates cash repayment.
interventions.additionality: Recovery is already widespread. Establish untreated-site/purchased-food baseline and causal lift beyond planned rollouts; no 60% factor applied to global disposed tonnage.
dependencies: baseline food throughput rather than revenue alone
existing recovery coverage and committed rollout
destination-specific disposal and recovery costs/emission factors
incremental product margin, staff costs and capex
overlaps: Prevented food cannot also earn full diversion credit.
Avoided upstream procurement and supplier Project Gigaton must not be added as separate company reductions.
Composting/AD can improve disposal impacts while still counting as food loss under the FLW standard.

fund_note: Principal repayment comes from contracted project cash flow, never monetized environmental damage unless an actual enforceable payment exists. No allocation of a billion-dollar fund or return guarantee is supported.
aggregation_note: Project Gigaton is supplier-reported avoided/reduced/sequestered activity across projects/time; it is not a deduction from Walmart annual Scope3 inventory. Do not subtract it. Technical possibility is distinct from external investor additionality.
